seaside.mp3.sourceDescription: Field recording of calm beach waves with birdsong and distant gulls, made on a spring morning in Walton-on-the-Naze, Essex, UK, using a Zoom H6 MSH-6 stereo microphone.
edits: Prepared from the openly available HQ MP3 preview; no login or full-quality original download was used.
Selected 12–96 seconds of the recording (84 seconds).
Applied a gentle 55 Hz high-pass and 7500 Hz low-pass to soften rumble and bright hiss.
Applied constant-gain loudness normalization near -24 LUFS, preserving natural wave dynamics; no synthesized waves or bird calls were added.
Encoded as 128 kbps stereo MP3 at 44100 Hz. Playback fade-in, fade-out and loop blending are handled by the website.

seaside-pcm.wav.sourceDescription: Field recording of calm beach waves with birdsong and distant gulls, made on a spring morning in Walton-on-the-Naze, Essex, UK, using a Zoom H6 MSH-6 stereo microphone.
seaside-pcm.wav.purpose: Compatibility fallback only when the normal MP3 recording cannot be decoded. Uncompressed PCM samples can be read directly without a platform MP3 decoder.
edits: Prepared from the same processed 84-second float PCM intermediate as seaside.mp3; it is not a second transcode of the final MP3.

The shared intermediate derives from the openly available HQ MP3 preview, selecting 12–96 seconds with the existing 55 Hz high-pass, 7500 Hz low-pass and constant-gain loudness adjustment. No synthesized waves or bird calls were added.

Downmixed both stereo channels to mono, resampled from 44100 Hz to 22050 Hz using the macOS Core Audio maximum-quality sample-rate converter, and converted to signed 16-bit little-endian PCM with dither.

No additional loudness normalization, dynamic compression or trimming was applied. The complete 84 seconds and natural wave dynamics are retained. Website playback supplies fades and the loop overlap.
